analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1561-1569, a documentation paragraph on byte-fallback detokenization in LocalTokenizerBridge.decode). The supplied units are base-text excerpts at lines 2465-3234, which the patch does not touch, so they are unchanged surrounding context. The patch is documentation-only: it adds no executable code and changes no controls. It does describe a source change (not supplied) in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/LocalTokenizerLoader.swift that releases trailing `<0xHH>` byte-fallback token runs. A partial run reads as U+FFFD and DetokenizerV2 holds it back. Security relevance is low: it affects output text correctness and streaming completeness, not encryption, attestation, authorization or cache scoping. It touches no threat-model assets or boundaries (A-001 sealing, TB-002 and TB-007 are unaffected). The decode path handles plaintext model output inside the provider process and adds no logging or persistence by itself. The actual Swift implementation was not supplied, so I cannot confirm the code matches the description. That includes whether a trailing-run release could emit malformed content or misbehave on adversarial token sequences, which would be a correctness or DoS concern at most. No regression is identified from the supplied evidence. The base excerpts include existing claims about prefix-cache (T-041), media caps and cluster behavior. None are modified by this PR, so I did not re-evaluate them.
